title: Attention kernel compatibility fuzzer and failure-mode simulator
creator: Ethan Chen
description:
Background: After incremental rollout of FlashAttention v3 variants we've observed rare, hard-to-reproduce regressions during mixed prefill+decode traffic: transient OOMs, kernel handshake timeouts, and latency spikes that do not reproduce deterministically in local or synthetic bench setups. Hypothesis: fragile inter-kernel handoff logic + workspace reuse + edge input shapes produce race conditions and memory fragmentation under tenant multiplexing.

Objective: Build an automated, configurable 'attention kernel compatibility fuzzer' that: (1) generates realistic multiplexed request traffic combining prefill and decode phases across a matrix of model shapes, precisions, batch sizes, and KV cache footprints; (2) injects controlled nondeterminism (timing jitter, allocation failures, GPU memory pressure, micro-bursts) to exercise race and fallback paths between FlashAttention v2/v3 kernels; (3) captures deterministic repro artifacts (trace, heap snapshot, kernel selection history, per-op timings) suitable for post-mortem and CI gating.

Deliverables: fuzz harness code in runtime repo, set of canonical scenarios, CI job for nightly fuzz runs against staging fleet, dashboards for fuzz-derived signals, and a prioritized triage list with remediation PRs.

Success criteria: reproductions for at least 3 previously non-deterministic incidents within 72h of running on staging; automated collection of traces and deterministic inputs for at least 90% of reproductions; addition of one low-latency mitigation (e.g., short handshake backoff or allocation fallback) with measurable reduction in incidence during subsequent canary runs.
tasks: Design harness interface and scenario language (shapes, precisions, workloads, fault injections)
Implement jitter/pressure injection primitives (timing jitter, forced alloc failure, simulated tiny workspace fragmentation)
Add kernel-selection tracepoint hooks and structured trace exporter (JSON line events + perf counters)
Create 12 canonical scenarios covering long-context prefill, interleaved prefill+decode, and small-batch hotpath
Integrate harness into runtime e2e CI (nightly on staging fleet) and a manual job for ad-hoc forensic runs
Build a Kibana/Grafana dashboard to surface fuzz reproductions and signal rates
Triage reproductions, file fixes, and validate mitigations via staged canary runs
acceptance_criteria: Harness can generate and persist deterministic repro inputs (exact seed + shape + payload) for any reproduced failure
CI job executes fuzz scenarios against a staging cluster and uploads traces to the observability bucket within 30 minutes
At least one intermittent regression from the last quarter is reliably reproduced by the harness
Telemetry dashboards surface reproduction counts, top failing scenarios, and per-tenant exposure
Sign-off from Runtime reliability lead and PM on rollout plan
comments: 2026-02-18 - Ethan Chen: Created ticket after oncall report 'prefill-decode OOM 2026-02-15' where capture was incomplete. Initial spike analysis suggests kernel handshake race. Opening this to get a reproducible harness rather than ad-hoc local repros.

2026-02-23 - Sofia Martinez: PoC harness skeleton pushed to PR #1426. It can simulate jittered request arrival and interleave prefill/decode across N simulated tenants. Needs richer fault primitives and structured trace export.

2026-02-26 - Marco Alvarez (Reviewer): Reviewed PR, requested: (1) deterministic seed support for RNGs so repros are repeatable, (2) attach memory-snapshot exporter on reproduction, (3) reduce default fuzz rate to avoid noisy CI failures. Also flagged that injecting forced alloc-failure can mask allocator differences between driver versions.

2026-03-02 - Sofia Martinez: Added deterministic seeds and trace uploader; implemented an 'alloc-fail-probability' parameter instead of forced OOM to surface fragile allocations without grinding the cluster. Ran 48h smoke—found 2 reproducible cases: one long-context OOM during v3->v2 handoff, and one 200ms latency spike correlated with workspace fragmentation on mixed precision workloads.

2026-03-05 - Priya Rao (PM): Prioritization call: focus first on reproducible OOM (higher customer impact) and add mitigations to prefill handshake backoff. Agreed to schedule canary tests before broad rollout. Also requested cost estimate for nightly fuzzing on staging fleet.

2026-03-08 - Sofia Martinez: Implemented lightweight mitigation: handshake backoff + a gated fallback allocation path that refuses to reuse remote workspace when fragmentation threshold exceeded. Running canary across 10% of staging nodes; early signal shows 75% reduction in repro rate for the targeted OOM scenario.

2026-03-09 - Ethan Chen: Planning follow-ups: (a) add a CI gating test that fails merges which increase probability of the top-5 fuzz scenarios, (b) schedule an incident postmortem for the original 2026-02-15 case and attach harness artifacts, (c) outreach to infra team to align allocator flags across driver versions. Marking task list updated, moving towards triage+fix PRs.
